description:
A social deduction game where players describe a secret word. Most players (Civilians) share the same word; two players (Undercovers) have a different but related word. Nobody is told which side they are on: each player sees only their own word and must work out from the others' descriptions whether it is the majority (Civilian) word or the minority (Undercover) word. GAME STRUCTURE: two Undercovers, four Civilians. WIN CONDITIONS: The Civilians win when both Undercovers have been voted out. The Undercovers win when exactly 1 Undercover and 1 Civilian remain, or when no Civilian remains. PHASES: (1) Description: Players take turns describing their word using one sentence, without revealing the word itself. (2) Voting: Players vote to eliminate a player they suspect holds the other word. The player with the most counted votes is out, and everyone is told whether that player was a Civilian or an Undercover; if the top vote is tied, one of the tied players is drawn at random and the draw is announced. Only players still in the game can be voted for; a vote for a player who is already out, or a vote that names no single player, counts as an abstention. STRATEGY: Describe your word vaguely enough not to give it away and specifically enough to show which word you hold. If the others' descriptions point to a different word than yours, you are probably an Undercover: then work out the majority word and blend in. 

 The players in this game are: {agent_names}.

role_goals.Civilian: Work out from the descriptions whether your word is the majority (Civilian) word or the minority (Undercover) word, describe it without giving it away, and help your side win the vote.
